notes: Answered strictly from public biography (b. 13 Oct 1925, Grantham, Lincolnshire; grocer's daughter to Alfred Roberts and Beatrice Stephenson; UK birth certificates of this era never record a time of birth, so any time — commonly cited as 9am — can only rest on family memory of a round hour, hence A1/A2/A3). Zero astrological material was consulted. Part D omitted entirely: those questions require having read a chart-based reading, which this blind exercise forbids opening. Notable judgment calls: A4/A5 - hospital record is thin; counted the Dec 2012 bladder-growth surgery and the 2002 stroke-related admissions ('two_three'/'one'), while true admission counts before/after office are not fully public. A6/A31 - later-life stroke (2002, fatal 2013) and documented dementia (revealed via Carol Thatcher's memoir and dramatized in 'The Iron Lady') justify head/nerves, but no formal mental-health treatment is on record so A31 stayed 'no'. A7/A8/A9 - childhood health, danger before age 8, and grandparent longevity are simply not part of the public record; picked the conservative middle/uncertain options rather than invent detail. A11 - father Alfred rose from one shop to two, plus alderman and eventually Mayor of Grantham, so 'prospered' fits better than 'steady'. A12/A13/C1/C8 - relationship with mother Beatrice and sister Muriel is consistently described as affectionately distant rather than warm (Thatcher's own quote about having 'nothing more to say' to her mother after age 15) rather than openly conflicted, so 'distant' plus a difficulty lean at low-to-moderate confidence. A17 - her greatest documented successes (MP, Cabinet minister, PM) were all achieved as an office-holder inside a party/electoral hierarchy rather than as an independent proprietor, hence 'under_authority' despite ultimately leading the government. A18 - restricted to two directly documented vocations: industrial research chemist (BX Plastics, J. Lyons) and barrister (tax law, called to the Bar 1953/54); did not add politics/writing since no matching category exists. A24/A27 - she was married to Denis from 1951 until his death in 2003 and outlived him, hence 'widowed' rather than 'married', with the marriage itself uniformly described as happy/supportive. A35/B6 - capped at the documented headline turning points (Oxford degree, marriage, birth of twins Mark and Carol, election to Parliament, Cabinet appointment, party leadership, becoming PM, the Falklands War, the 1984 Brighton bombing assassination attempt, the 1990 forced resignation, the 2002 strokes, and Denis's 2003 death); no reliable month is public for the 2002 strokes so '03' is an estimate flagged here. C4/C5/C10 - long journeys, eyesight, and confinement are essentially undocumented as either good or bad, so low-confidence conservative defaults were chosen rather than invented drama. C11/C12 - chosen as clear 'difficulty' given the extensively documented opposition she faced (miners' and other strikes, IRA targeting including the Brighton bombing, poll-tax unrest, and the 1990 cabinet revolt that ended her premiership).
